title: Four is enough

feedback.title: Deliberately lose this trick
feedback.summary: You are exactly on target: 4 taken, 4 estimated. The three loses to the queen and avoids an unwanted fifth trick.
points: You act last, so the queen wins this trick if you play the three. No unseen response can change this trick.
The king would win and put you above target. Exact means four, not at least four.
Keeping four now does not guarantee the final result. You still need to avoid tricks in the unresolved remainder.

feedback.title: A winning card can be the wrong decision
feedback.summary: The king wins an unwanted fifth trick. You started exactly on target at 4 of 4; taking this trick would put you above it.
points: All three other cards are lower Hearts and you act last, so the king cannot avoid winning here.
The legal three of Hearts would deliberately lose instead. Once you take five, later losses cannot reduce your taken count back to four.

author_notes: EC-043 intentional-loss case. Same visible cards as _001 isolate how the exact target changes the decision. Ratings address this trick, not guaranteed success through the rest of the hand. Opponent estimates (EC-055/D-027) are chosen for the same reason the taken counts are: to keep the decision about South's own exact target. North wins this trick in the reviewed intentional-loss line, so North estimates 4 with 2 taken — still needing another trick afterwards — rather than a value this trick would complete. Deliberately losing here is therefore not also a decision about North's contract.
